questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of an overdraft?
options: An arrangement allowing a business to withdraw more than it has in its account, up to a limit
A fixed sum borrowed and repaid with interest over an agreed period
An arrangement to pay a supplier 30 to 90 days after delivery
Renting an asset rather than buying it
questions.why: An overdraft is short-term flexibility: you pay interest only on what you use, which makes it ideal for bridging a cash flow gap and expensive as long-term finance.
whyNot: That is a loan.
That is trade credit.
That is leasing.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: renting an asset rather than buying it, paying a regular charge for its use?
options: Leasing
Trade credit
Share capital
A grant
questions.why: Leasing avoids a large upfront payment and often includes maintenance. Over the asset's life it costs more than buying, and you never own it.
whyNot: Trade credit is delayed payment to a supplier.
Share capital is finance raised by selling part ownership.
A grant is money that does not have to be repaid.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: a wealthy individual who invests their own money in a small business?
options: Business angel
Venture capitalist
Peer-to-peer lender
Shareholder in a plc
questions.why: Angels bring experience, contacts and credibility as well as cash, and they take equity and expect some involvement.
whyNot: A venture capitalist is a specialist firm investing other people's money, usually in larger sums.
Peer-to-peer lenders lend rather than take equity, through a platform.
A plc shareholder buys shares on a public market, usually with no involvement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of trade credit?
options: An arrangement to pay a supplier a set period after receiving goods
A loan from a bank secured on stock
Selling goods to customers on credit
A government payment that need not be repaid
questions.why: Typically 30 to 90 days. It is effectively an interest-free short-term loan from the supplier, which is why working capital management relies on it.
whyNot: That is a secured loan.
That is offering credit to customers, which uses up cash rather than providing it.
That is a grant.

questions.stem: A business wants to buy premises expected to last 25 years. Which finance is most appropriate?
options: A long-term bank loan or a mortgage
An overdraft
Trade credit
A short-term loan repayable in six months
questions.why: Match the term of the finance to the life of the asset. A long-lived asset should be funded over a long period so repayments come out of the returns it generates.
whyNot: The classic error. An overdraft is expensive and repayable on demand, so funding a building with it is dangerous.
Trade credit covers goods for resale over weeks, not property over decades.
Repaying the cost of a building in six months would cripple cash flow.

questions.stem: What is the main disadvantage of raising finance through share capital?
options: Ownership and control are diluted, and new shareholders share future profits
Interest must be paid every month
The finance must be repaid within five years
Only sole traders can use it
questions.why: There is no interest and no repayment, and the cost is permanent: new shareholders own part of the business, expect dividends and can outvote the founder.
whyNot: Shares carry no interest. Dividends are discretionary.
Share capital is permanent; it is not repaid.
Only companies can issue shares. A sole trader cannot.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a source from a method of finance?
options: A bank is a source; a loan is a method
A loan is a source; a bank is a method
They mean the same thing
Sources are internal and methods are external
questions.why: The specification separates who the money comes from (the source) from the form it takes (the method). Mixing them up is a common and avoidable error.
whyNot: This reverses them.
They are distinct, and the specification treats them separately.
Both sources and methods here are external.

questions.stem: Why might a business prefer debt finance to equity finance even though it has to pay interest?
options: The owners keep full control and keep all the future profit beyond the interest
Debt never has to be repaid
Debt is always cheaper than equity in every circumstance
Lenders share the losses if the business does badly
questions.why: Interest is a fixed cost, so once it is paid the remaining upside belongs to the owners, and no ownership is given away. Equity investors share the upside forever.
whyNot: Debt must be repaid, with interest.
Debt is often cheaper, and not always; a highly geared business faces high rates.
Lenders must be paid regardless, so the risk stays with the business.

questions.stem: A high-risk start-up with no revenue yet needs $500,000. Why is equity more appropriate than debt?
options: It has no cash flow to service repayments, and equity requires none
Equity finance is always cheaper
Banks are not allowed to lend to start-ups
Equity investors cannot lose money
questions.why: Debt demands repayment from month one. A business with no revenue cannot service it, so debt would sink it. Equity investors accept the risk in exchange for a share of the upside.
whyNot: Equity is often the most expensive finance in the long run, because investors keep a share of all future profit.
They can lend, and they are usually unwilling to without security or cash flow.
Equity investors can lose everything they put in; that is the risk they are paid for.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a drawback of crowd funding?
options: The campaign is public, so failure is visible, and it needs a compelling story
It always requires giving up control of the business
It is only available to large companies
The money must be repaid with interest
questions.why: Crowd funding doubles as marketing and market testing, and a campaign that does not reach its target fails in public, which can damage credibility.
whyNot: Depending on the model, backers may receive a product or a reward rather than equity.
It is mainly used by small businesses and start-ups.
Many crowd funding models involve rewards or pre-orders rather than repayable debt.

questions.stem: Why does trade credit matter especially to a business in an import-dependent economy?
options: Suppliers offering 60 days are financing its working capital at no cost
Imported goods cannot be bought any other way
Trade credit removes the need for a bank account
It eliminates the effect of exchange rate movements
questions.why: Long credit terms on imported stock fund the gap between paying for goods and selling them, interest free. Losing the facility by paying late would hurt more than a change in a loan rate.
whyNot: They can be bought for cash; credit is a financing choice.
A bank account is still needed to pay the supplier eventually.
Credit delays payment; it does not remove currency risk, and may even increase it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of collateral?
options: An asset pledged as security for a loan, which the lender can take on default
The interest charged on a loan
The period over which a loan is repaid
A payment made to arrange a loan
questions.why: Collateral reduces the lender's risk, which is why a business with assets can borrow more cheaply, and why a start-up without them struggles.
whyNot: That is the interest.
That is the loan term.
That is an arrangement fee.
